text: Git branching helps developers work on different tasks without affecting the main code. A common practice is to create a feature branch for each new task, such as adding a feature or fixing a bug. This keeps the main branch stable and safe. When the work is finished, you merge the feature branch back into the main branch. Before merging, teams often open a pull request so others can review the changes. This version control workflow makes collaboration easier and reduces mistakes. By using branches, merges, and pull requests, teams can develop software together in a clear and organized way.
